 J U D G M E N T This petition Under section 166 MV act is filed seeking compensation of .40,00,000/ SCCH13 3 MVC.1441/2019C for the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. It is stated that on 15082018 about 8.30 a.m., the Petitioner was riding a motorcycle bearing No.KA01EH1881 from Chokkanahalli to Hennur via Marenahalli, near Marenahalli Anjinappa house, the driver of JCB bearing Reg.No.KA53MF0606 (hereinafter called as offending vehicle)
drove the same in high speed and in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle of Petitioner from behind.
Due to the accident Petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
He was immediately taken to Manasa hospital, then shifted to Hosmat hospital, later he was shifted to Sanjaygandhi hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he has taken treatment as an inpatient.
He is suffering from permanent disability and unable to lead normal life as earlier.
It is claimed that Petitioner has spent .2,40,000/ for treatment, medicines, conveyance and other charges.
At the time of SCCH 13 4 MVC.1441/2019C accident, Petitioner was a private worker and was earning .40,000/ to 45,000/ p.m.
Due to accidental injuries he has lost his earning capacity and income.
As the accident was caused due to negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle, it is requested to award compensation from the Respondent No.1 to 3 being the insurer, owner and driver.
3. In response to the petition notice, the Respondent No.1 to 3 have appeared before the court through their counsel and filed their written statement.
4. The Respondent No.1Insurance company has filed its written statement denying the petition averments.
It has admitted the issuance of policy and its validity as on the date of accident.
However, its liability is subject to terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.
It has also contended that the owner of the alleged offending vehicle has not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) of MV Act.
It has contended that SCCH13 5 MVC.1441/2019C the insurer of motorcycle bearing No.KA01 EH1881 are necessary parties to the proceedings.
It has denied the negligence of the driver of offending vehicle in causing the accident.
It is stated that accident was taken place due to the negligence of Petitioner and he was not holding valid DL.

It is contended that Sri.Manjunath M vs Liberty Gen.Insurance Co.Ltd on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36708043/

It has contended that the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective DL at the time of accident.
It has also denied the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, avocation and income of the Petitioner, and the future expenses claimed by him and disability suffered by him.
For all these, it has prayed for dismissal of the petition.
5. Respondent No.2RC owner has filed his written statement denying the contents of petition averments.

He has admitted that he is the RC owner of offending vehicle and the same was insured with Respondent No.1 and policy was valid as on the date of accident SCCH13 6 MVC.1441/2019C and the driver had valid DL.
It is contended that the accident was not due to negligence of driver of the offending vehicle, but it was the negligence of Petitioner himself, as he hit the standing vehicle.
He has denied the other allegations of the petition averments and prayed for dismissal of the petition.
6. Respondent No.3 Driver of offending vehicle has filed his written statement denying the contents of petition averments.
He has admitted that Respondent No.2 is the RC owner of offending vehicle and the same was insured with Respondent No.1 and policy was valid as on the date of accident and he was holding valid DL.
It is contended that the accident was not due to his negligence, but it was the negligence of Petitioner himself, as he hit the standing vehicle.
He has denied the other allegations of the petition averments and prayed for dismissal of the petition.

On the basis of the above pleadings, the following Issues were framed :-
1.Whether the Petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injury in RTA on 15 082018 at 8.30 a.m. in front of Puttanna house, Marenahalli, Bagaluru Post, Jala Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluk, Bengaluru District, due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the JCB bearing No.KA53MF0606?
2. Whether the Petitioner proves that he is entitled for the compensation as claimed?

If so, to what extent and from whom?
3. What order or award ?

8. In order to prove the claim, the Petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and in support of his case, 3 witnesses are examined as PW2 to 4 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.22 respectively.
9. The Respondent No.1 has examined the ARTO, K.R.Puram as RW1 and got marked the document at Ex.R.1.
Further the official of Respondent No.1 is examined as RW2.

Owner of SCCH 13 8 MVC.1441/2019C offending vehicle is examined as RW3 and got marked the documents at Ex.R.2 to 4.
10.
I have heard the counsel on both sides and have perused the material on record.

My findings to the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
R E A S O N S 12.
ISSUE NO.1:
In order to prove his claim, Petitioner relied on the police and medical records.
PW1 is the injured and the direct witness to the incident.

He has deposed that on 15082018 about 8.30 a.m., he was riding a motorcycle bearing No.KA01 EH1881 from Chokkanahalli to Hennur via Marenahalli, near Marenahalli Anjinappa house, the driver of JCB bearing Reg.No.KA 53MF0606 drove the same in high speed and in rash and negligent manner and dashed SCCH13 9 MVC.1441/2019C against the motorcycle from behind.
Due to the accident, he has sustained grievous injuries.
It is stated that the the accident was solely due to rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle.
13. In support of his claim he has produced copy of FIR at Ex.P.1, complaint at Ex.P.2, charge sheet at Ex.P.3, Wound certificate at Ex.P.4 and IMV report at Ex.P.5.
As per wound certificate he has sustained Type 3B compound fracture of left proximal tibia and left radial neck fracture.
14. The Respondentinsurance company has contended that the it was the negligence of Petitioner himself and suggested that due to his own negligence he dashed to the offending JCB.
By relying on the IMV report and the damages, it is contended that the motorcycle has dashed the JCB.
RespondentInsurance company has examined the ARTO and its official as RW1 and 2 respectively.
But no evidence are adduced with regard to SCCH13 10 MVC.1441/2019C negligence.
Respondent No.2 - RC owner examined himself as RW3 and contended that there was no negligence of his driver.
He admits that his driver did not give any complaint alleging negligence of Petitioner.
15. Both have not produced spot sketch.
According to the Petitioner's case JCB came and hit the motorcycle from behind.
Complaint has been given immediately on the same day and the chargesheet is filed against the driver of JCB alleging his negligence.
More over the driver of offending JCB had no DL to drive the offending vehicle.
16. There are no materials on record to disprove the Petitioner's evidence and to prove the contention of the Respondents.
The evidence of PW1 corroborates with the documents produced by him.
There is nothing elicited to disprove the negligence on the part of the offending vehicle.
After the investigation, police have filed the charge sheet against the driver of the offending SCCH 13 11 MVC.1441/2019C vehicle and the copy of the charge sheet is produced at Ex.P.3.
From all the above documents it is clear that the Petitioner sustained injuries in road traffic accident that occurred only due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending JCB.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.

As the salary was not constant and he was working for a daily wages,
it would be just and reasonable to consider his monthly income as .16,000/.

has deposed that he has gone through the discharge summary and found the Petitioner has sustained Type 3 B compound fracture of left proximal tibia and left radial neck fracture and he was operated with: a) External fixator application to left lower limb b) External fixator removal done and c) ORIF with plates and screws and bone grafting for left proximal tibia non union done.

On perusal of evidence, there is no disability due to neck injury.

By considering the evidence of PW1 & 2, injuries sustained by the Petitioner, age and SCCH13 15 MVC.1441/2019C avocation of the Petitioner, the functional disability is assessed at 15%.
21.
The Petitioner has stated that he was aged about 32 years, in support of his age he has produced DL, which shows his date of birth as 01011986.
Hence, his age is considered as 32 years as on the date of accident.
Therefore, the proper multiplier applicable to the case on hand is 16.

On the basis of these, Loss of future earnings due to permanent disability will be as .16,000x12x16x15%=
.4,60,800/.
22. Pain and sufferings:

So far as the compensation under nonpecuniary damages are concerned,
considering the fact that the Petitioner has suffered Type 3 B compound fracture of left proximal tibia and left radial neck fracture and was inpatient for a period of 42 days in 3 occasions which caused him to immeasurable mental agony and pain, I am of the opinion that an amount of .50,000/ would be just and fair SCCH13 16 MVC.1441/2019C compensation under the head pain and sufferings.
23. Loss of amenities of life:
For loss of amenities of life undoubtedly Petitioner is sure to suffer in his day today activities and face hardships.
Hence, Petitioner is awarded .20,000/ under loss of amenities of life.
24. Medical expenses:
Under the pecuniary damages, expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization and medicines, the Petitioner has relied on medical bills at Ex.P.6 and 13 for .92,786/ and .2,753/.
The counsel for insurance company and RC owner have cross examined the PW1 regarding genuineness of the medical bills.
But it was denied by PW1 that the bills are created.
As the medical bill appears to be genuine, by considering the all medical bills, Petitioner is awarded .95,539/ towards Medical Expenses.
25. Future medical expenses:

Petitioner has stated that he require another SCCH13 17 MVC.1441/2019C .2,00,000/ for further treatment and he has produced Ex.P.14 - estimation for removal of implants, issued by Manasa hospital, Bengaluru.
It shows that on 06022019, the Petitioner has undergone surgery for removal of implants and the approximate hospitalization charges was .55,000/.
PW 2doctor has stated that the Petitioner needs removal of implants and it is part of treatment.
In the absence of clear estimation of the future expenses, it would be proper to award .20,000/ towards Future medical expenses.
26. Conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges:
Petitioner has not produced the Discharge summary.

However, on perusal of case sheets, it shows that Petitioner was treated as an inpatient at Sanjaygandhi hospital, Bengaluru from 1508 2018 to 25082018, from 12102018 to 2010 2018, from 06022019 to 27022019 i.e. totally for a period of 42 days.

sentences.text: The Petitioner has examined the Cab driver as PW4 to show that he was hired a Cab for pick up and drop for treatment from his nature place to Sanjaygandhi hospital.
The Petitioner has produced 18 trip sheets/ cash bills at Ex.P.6(a), which shows that he has incurred .53,400/ towards taxi charges.
During crossexamination, PW4 has stated that since it was agreed to pay consolidated amount per trip, he has not mentioned Kilometers in the bills.
During detailed crossexamination it is found that the RC owner is different and the bills are issued by the driver only.
The bills are produced for total 18 trips.
He says that the handwriting on the bills are not of him.
Only the signatures are of PW.4.
Petitioner has produced only 8 OPD sheets hence all the taxi bills cannot be considered.
There are no supportive documents to show that on all the trip dates he had visited the Sanjaygandhi hospital.

Hence, by considering number of days admission in the hospital, number of OPD SCCH13 19 MVC.1441/2019C records and other documents, Petitioner is awarded .60,000/ under the head of conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges.
28. Loss of earning during laid up period:

With regard to loss of earnings during treatment,
considering 42 days admission in the hospital as inpatient and around 45 days for rest is considered and loss of earnings during treatment is calculated for 3 months.

As the monthly income of the Petitioner is already considered as .16,000/ per month, loss of earning during laid up period would be .48,000/.
29.

30.Liability:
Respondent No.1 Insurance company denied its liability to indemnify the claim as the driver of JCB was not holding valid DL.
It is alleged that the driver had only license to LMV non transport and tractor and not for JCB.
Official from the insurance company is examined as RW2 and he has stated that the driver Upendra Kumar is chargesheeted U/s.3(a) R/w 181 of MV Act for not holding valid DL at the time of accident.

sentences.text: ARTO is examined as RW1 and he has stated that since the JCB is a specially built vehicle, one shall obtain DL for construction equipment as special category to run JCB.
He has produced DL extract of Respondent No.3 at Ex.R.1.
According to which SCCH13 21 MVC.1441/2019C he had DL to drive motorcycle with gear, LMV and tractor.

Even after crossexamination of RW.1 and suggested with regard to Central Motor Vehicles Rules, witness says that JCB is treated as construction equipment and it is classified as both transport and non transport vehicle.
He denied the suggestion that according to Rule 2(ca) of Central Motor Vehicles Rules 1989, one with LMV license can drive JCB which is construction equipment.
32. Respondent No.2 RC owner examined himself as RW3 and stated that the insurance was valid as on the date of accident and the Respondent No.3 driver had valid DL to drive JCB.
He has produced policy copy along with RC copy, policy copy and DL of Respondent No.3.
During cross examination he states that person having DL for LMV can drive the vehicle having unladen weight of 7500 Kgs.
But he admits that police have filed chargesheet alleging that Respondent No.3 had no DL and he was also the accused.
He admits that he did not challenged the chargesheet SCCH13 22 MVC.1441/2019C and paid the fine after pleading guilty before the Magistrate.

According to this,
Respondent No.2 has admitted that he had handed over the vehicle to a person who had no valid DL.
33.

At the time of argument, Petitioner and Respondent No.2 and 3 have filed written argument and Respondent No.2 and 3 have produced Government of India Notification dated 19061992 and Judgment of Hon'ble High Court dated 07022014 in MFA. No.21800/2010, AIR 2017 SC 3688 (Mukund Dewangan case) and Judgment of Hon'lbe High Court dated 0911 2020 in MFA.6789/2010

and argued that the High Court and Supreme Court have held that the driver of JCB who had driving license to drive a light motor vehicle was indeed authorized to drive the JCB and the Hon'ble High Court has upheld that order of tribunal fixing the liability to pay compensation upon the insurer.
By the above Judgments and Rules, it is clear that the person having DL for LMV is authorized to drive JCB and hence the contention of the Respondentinsurance company cannot be accepted.
In view of these discussion, I hold that the insurance company cannot deny its liability to indemnify the claim and shall pay the compensation to the Petitioner.

Since the negligence of Respondent No.3 is proved, Respondent No.1 to 3 being insurer, RC owner and driver of the offending JCB are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation with interest at 6% p.a. to the Petitioner as issuance of policy and subsistence of policy is not disputed.
With these observation I answer Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
35. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos. 1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following:
